question: A school district in Oklahoma showed up on ICE's 287(g) list in March. What happened?
answerMarkdown:
**About this data:** This answer draws on [287(g) Watch](https://287g.recoveredfactory.net), a civic data project of Recovered Factory. Its data tracks ICE's published 287(g) roster. The site has a page for every agency and state, and the full data is free to [download](https://287g.recoveredfactory.net/en/downloads). For questions or corrections, write to davideads@recoveredfactory.net. Please check the work, because the source data (mostly ICE's) has known gaps.

## What the roster shows

The agency is almost certainly the [Caney Valley Public Schools Police Department](https://287g.recoveredfactory.net/en/agency/caney-valley-public-schools-police-department-ok). It is the only school-district agency in Oklahoma that has ever shown up in ICE's roster. All the facts below are from the roster snapshots, which run through 2026-11-24.

- **Model:** ICE listed it under the [Task Force Model](https://287g.recoveredfactory.net/en/model/taskforce). That is the broadest 287(g) model, under which officers can stop, question and arrest people in the community, not only people already in custody.
- **Location and type:** ICE lists it in Washington County. ICE labels its agency type as "Municipality," not a school district.
- **Signed date:** ICE's roster gives 2026-03-13. ICE doesn't say whose signature that date marks.
- **Added:** It first appeared in the roster snapshot of 2026-03-17.
- **Removed:** It was gone from the snapshot of 2026-03-18, one day later. 287(g) Watch now marks it terminated.

So the listing lasted about a day. Those dates are snapshot dates, and the real changes may have come days earlier.

## What the data can't tell you

- **Why it was removed.** The roster doesn't say whether the district backed out, ICE pulled the listing, or the entry was an error or a premature posting.
- **Whether it ever operated.** There is no agreement document on file for this agency, so I can't say what, if anything, was signed. The data also doesn't show any enforcement activity under it.
- **Press coverage.** 287(g) Watch's news collection for Oklahoma only covers August 2026 onward, and nothing in it matches Caney Valley. I haven't searched the web, so I can't say whether local outlets covered it.

## Wider context

That week was busy in Oklahoma. The roster shows 9 agencies added in March 2026, mostly small-town police departments and sheriff's offices, all under the Task Force Model. Among them are [Colbert](https://287g.recoveredfactory.net/en/agency/colbert-police-department-ok), [Caddo](https://287g.recoveredfactory.net/en/agency/caddo-police-department-ok) and [Okmulgee County Sheriff's Office](https://287g.recoveredfactory.net/en/agency/okmulgee-county-sheriffs-office-ok). Oklahoma now has 132 active agencies.

I can search the news, in English and Spanish, for why Caney Valley's listing was pulled. I can also pull Oklahoma's state summary or the rest of Washington County's agencies.

*Attribution: Recovered Factory / 287(g) Watch (287g.recoveredfactory.net), CC BY 4.0.*
